outcome: Delivery preferences (vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 237 nulliparous pregnant women in their second trimester without an absolute indication for cesarean, attending antenatal follow-up at Ankara University Faculty of Medicine.
finding: The majority of nulliparous pregnant women (93.2%) preferred vaginal delivery, while a smaller proportion (6.8%) preferred delivery by cesarean section.
mod_finding: The study found that 93.2% of nulliparous pregnant women preferred vaginal delivery, and 6.8% preferred cesarean section.
cross-section timing: During the second trimester of pregnancy, between May 2014 and February 2015
gest_age: Second trimester (of pregnancy for the participants)
